body:
Where Does Rain Go?: 1. From the clouds. 2. With their roots. 3. The sun warms it, the water goes up into the air, and the puddle gets smaller until it is gone. 4. Drawing shows rain drops falling on a plant.
Our Rain Cup: 1. Tuesday (5 is more than 2). 2. Wednesday (3 is less than 5). 3. Tuesday. 4. Drawing shows the cup with water up to line 5.
Where Did the Puddle Go?: the first picture shows a big puddle; the second shows a small puddle or a dry spot with the sun. The student tells it in order: the puddle was big, the sun warmed it, the puddle got smaller or dried up.
Rain and Water Check: 1. From the clouds. 2. Plants (also trees, grass, animals, people). 3. Thursday (4 is more than 1). 4. The sun warms it and the water goes into the air. 5. Drawing shows a puddle getting smaller or gone, with the sun.
Scoring tip: kindergartners do not need the word evaporate; "the sun dried it up" or "the water went into the air" is Got it! A student who says the puddle "went into the ground" is partly right (some water does soak in) and is Getting there if they do not mention the sun.
title: Answer key: Rain and Water
